column4: Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 Countries
column10: [This article explores Rhenium production by top 10 countries. You can skip the detailed industry analysis and jump straight to the Top 5 Countries by Rhenium Production.With an impressively high melting point, superb heat resistance, and extraordinary electrical conductivity, Rhenium finds extensive use in aerospace applications, where it is incorporated into high-temperature superalloys. This metal, with an atomic number of 72 and a relative atomic mass of 178.49, possesses remarkable properties that set it apart.Rhenium’s impressive melting point of 2233°C and boiling point of 4603°C make it highly resistant to extreme temperatures. With a density of 13310 kgm-3, Rhenium is known for its exceptional density among metals. Notably, it showcases a low electrical resistivity of 300 nΩm, combined with a high Young's modulus of 78 GPa, making it an ideal choice for applications requiring both electrical conductivity and mechanical strength. Furthermore, Rhenium exhibits a heat capacity of 25.73 J/K/mol. Despite its relatively low natural abundance of 5.3 ppm, Rhenium stands out with its excellent thermal conductivity of 23 W/m/K.It also serves as a catalyst in various chemical reactions and plays a vital role in advanced electronics through its application in electrical contacts. Rhenium's scarcity and specialized applications contribute to its significance in the global market.Industry leaders such as BHP Group (NYSE:BBL), Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM), and Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) can shape the future of the resources sector through sustainable practices and responsible mining. BHP Group (NYSE:BBL) operates globally in mining and petroleum, while Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) practices responsible mining worldwide. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) focuses on copper, gold, and molybdenum production. With diverse portfolios, including iron ore, copper, and coal, BHP Group (NYSE:BBL) contributes to the industry. Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) invests in communities and supplies gold. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) prioritizes safety, environmental stewardship, and community engagement. By conforming to environment-friendly and ethical practices, these companies can drive positive change and inspire others in the industry to follow suit.Story continuesFrom Scarcity to Success: Global Rhenium MarketThe worldwide production of Rhenium experienced a subtle decline, as the production volume dipped to approximately 59 metric tons in 2021, which decreased from the previous level of 59.3 metric tons recorded in 2020.Rhenium continues to play a vital role in jet engines and turbine blades, as well as finding applications in catalysts for oil refining within the petrochemical sector. Moreover, the healthcare industry utilizes Rhenium in various capacities, despite its overall decrease in demand.According to the "Global Rhenium Market 2022-2026" report, the Rhenium market is projected to witness substantial growth, with its market share anticipated to grow by $80.27 million by 2026. This growth is expected to occur at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.12% from 2021 to 2026. The market structure of the Rhenium industry is fragmented, with various players operating in the market.Technavio notes that the industry has shown a year-on-year growth of 12.38%, indicating a positive upward trend. In terms of regional analysis, the Rhenium market encompasses North America, Europe, APAC (Asia-Pacific), South America, and the Middle East and Africa. Among these regions, North America holds the largest market share, contributing approximately 65% to the overall market. Key consumer countries driving the demand for Rhenium include the United States, Canada, China, Russia, and Germany.Prominent Rhenium Market Trends To WatchAs the market for Rhenium continues to evolve, several key trends are expected to shape its trajectory. These trends include:Aerospace demand boost: Increasingly, Rhenium alloys are sought after in the aerospace and aviation sectors due to their heat resistance and mechanical strength.Energy sector advancements: Rhenium catalysts are gaining traction in fuel cells and hydrogen production, aligning with the growing demand for renewable energy technologies.Electronics integration: Rhenium's excellent electrical and thermal conductivity properties make it valuable in microelectronics and semiconductors, catering to the expanding electronics industry.Catalyst significance: Rhenium catalysts are finding wider applications in the chemical industry, particularly in petroleum refining, aromatics production, and catalytic reforming.Healthcare sector driving Rhenium-188 demand: The growing use of Rhenium-188 in the healthcare industry is set to generate promising opportunities for the Rhenium market in the foreseeable future.Rhenium-188 in nuclear medicine: Derived from the tungsten-188 generator, Rhenium-188 is a powerful radioisotope emitting high-energy radiation. It is extensively employed in nuclear medicine to produce radiopharmaceuticals used in therapeutic applications such as oncology, interventional radiology, cardiology, and other treatments.Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 CountriesPhoto by Artyom korshunov on UnsplashMethodologyOur assessment of Rhenium production among various countries involved a meticulous ranking methodology. To ensure the utmost reliability and accuracy of our findings, we extensively researched data from trusted sources such as The United States Geological Survey (USGS). By utilizing production percentages from E3S Web of Conferences, we calculated the production output of France and Germany specifically for the year 2020.  We then ranked the countries in ascending order according to their actual Rhenium production quantities, measured in metric tons. 10. ArmeniaMetric Tons: 0.26Armenia is known for its significant production of the rare metal Rhenium, especially for aerospace and defense industries utilization. The country's major Rhenium production is concentrated from the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine. Armenia's geological conditions and its abundant reserves of copper and molybdenum make it an ideal location for the production of Rhenium. The country's Rhenium production has played a vital role in boosting its economy and making it a significant player in the global metals market.9. KazakhstanMetric Tons: 1Kazakhstan's Rhenium production remained consistent at 1 metric ton in both 2015 and 2016, and this level was maintained in 2021 as well. The country implements a Rhenium recovery process that involves utilizing a sulphuric acid scrubbing solution. A noteworthy aspect of Kazakhstan's Rhenium production is the copper concentrates discovered in Zhezkazgan, which contain up to 30 grams per ton (g/t) of Rhenium.These deposits are globally recognized as the richest known sources of Rhenium. The abundance of Rhenium in these copper concentrates highlights the significant role played by Kazakhstan in meeting the demand for this valuable element, which finds applications in various industrial sectors.8. ChinaMetric Tons: 2.5Many producers in China have traditionally used the Kennecott Process for Rhenium extraction; there is an exception with Jiangxi Copper Corporation. The Kennecott Process has been widely used in the industry for over 40 years to extract Rhenium.In this process, exhaust gasses from the molybdenum roasting circuit are washed with water to produce perrhenic acid. The solution is then treated with chemicals like NaOH and Ca(ClO)2 to remove contaminants and adjust the pH. The solution undergoes ion exchange processing, where a resin adsorbs the Rhenium, which is later stripped using hydrochloric acid. The recovered Rhenium can further undergo purification steps, including recrystallization.Jiangxi Copper Corporation, which was the largest Rhenium producer in China in 2016, has developed and implemented its own production process. Their method includes solvent extraction of the scrubbing liquid, stripping of the organic solvent, purification, and crystallization of NH4ReO4, resulting in a Rhenium yield of up to 92%. Therefore, while the majority of Chinese producers employ the Kennecott Process, Jiangxi Copper Corporation has adopted a different approach to Rhenium recovery.7. Republic of KoreaMetric Tons: 2.8According to USGS, the Republic of Korea produced approximately 2.8 metric tons of Rhenium in 2020 and 2021. South Korea's production of Rhenium underscores its industrial prowess and technological advancements. The country's emphasis on innovation and research has enabled it to become a key player in the global supply chain of this valuable metal. With a focus on meeting market demands and supporting various sectors, South Korea continues to contribute significantly to the production and availability of Rhenium worldwide.6. FranceMetric Tons: 4.24In 2020, France produced approximately 4.24 tons of Rhenium. The country has emerged as one of the leading producers of Rhenium products within Western Europe. This growth can be attributed to several factors, including the expansion of the aerospace industry, a thriving automotive sector, increased applications in the biomedical field, and the utilization of Rhenium powder and salt crystals. These factors have collectively contributed to the notable increase in Rhenium production within France.Click to continue reading and see Rhenium Production by Country: Top 5 Countries.Suggested Articles:10 Best Gold Royalty Stocks to Buy Now10 Small-Cap Mining Stocks Hedge Funds Are Avoiding12 Best Silver Mining Stocks To Buy NowDisclosure: none. column4: UPDATE 1-Peru sees copper projects on track, to stay ahead of Congo on output
column10: [(Adds graphic, comparative data with Congo)By Marco AquinoLIMA, June 1 (Reuters) - Peru is bullish about holding on as the world's No. 2 copper producer with key projects set to move forward, its mining minister said on Thursday amid a stern challenge from fast growing rival Democratic Republic of Congo.The Andean country has seen its position come under threat by the rapid emergence of Congo, which almost matched Peru's copper production and exports last year though it fell just short on both counts, official data from both countries show.A report earlier this week said that Congo could grab the No. 2 spot as Peru's output growth stalled within the next few years. Neighboring Andean producer Chile remains the world's dominant producer and supplier of the red metal.Both Peru and Chile have seen copper production plateau, linked to political and regulatory uncertainty.Peru's Mining Minister Oscar Vera said the country's copper industry could boost output of the key metal needed for the global electrification shift, adding that mines worth some $6 billion were set to come online over the next two years.Vera said Peru mining projects on the horizon include the $1.5 billion Zafranal mine and the $2.5 billion Yanacocha Sulfuros project controlled by Newmont Mining Corp."The general manager (of Yanacocha) was with us a few weeks ago, and we were told of their decision to continue moving forward and that they plan to invest around $400 million through the end of the year," Vera said.Newmont did not respond to a request for comment.Vera also said government authorization would be coming soon for an investment of around $1.3 billion to expand the Aluminum Corp-controlled Toromocho mine.The Andean country has some $53 billion in pending mining projects, according to government data, but most are long term and have been delayed amid social and political unrest.(Reporting by Marco Aquino; Writing by Kylie Madry; Editing by David Alire Garcia, Edmund Klamann and Chizu Nomiyama)]

column4: An Intrinsic Calculation For Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) Suggests It's 25% Undervalued
column10: [Key InsightsNewmont's estimated fair value is US$53.88 based on 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to EquityNewmont's US$40.68 share price signals that it might be 25% undervalued The US$57.12 analyst price target for NEM is 6.0% more than our estimate of fair valueHow far off is Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by projecting its future cash flows and then discounting them to today's value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Believe it or not, it's not too difficult to follow, as you'll see from our example!We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. If you still have some burning questions about this type of valuation, take a look at the Simply Wall St analysis model. View our latest analysis for Newmont The CalculationWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To begin with, we have to get estimates of the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, so we need to discount the sum of these future cash flows to arrive at a present value estimate:10-year free cash flow (FCF) estimate2023202420252026202720282029203020312032 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$1.45bUS$1.68bUS$2.20bUS$2.98bUS$3.32bUS$3.56bUS$3.77bUS$3.95bUS$4.10bUS$4.24bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x12Analyst x12Analyst x9Analyst x2Analyst x1Est @ 7.43%Est @ 5.83%Est @ 4.72%Est @ 3.93%Est @ 3.39% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 9.1% US$1.3kUS$1.4kUS$1.7kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.0kUS$2.0kUS$1.9kUS$1.8k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$18bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.1%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 9.1%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2032 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$4.2b× (1 + 2.1%) ÷ (9.1%– 2.1%) = US$62bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$62b÷ ( 1 + 9.1%)10= US$26bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$44b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$40.7, the company appears a touch undervalued at a 25% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Newmont as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 9.1%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.182. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for NewmontStrengthDebt is not viewed as a risk.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Metals and Mining market.Shareholders have been diluted in the past year.OpportunityExpected to breakeven next year.Has sufficient cash runway for more than 3 years based on current free cash flows.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatDividends are not covered by cash flow.Moving On:Whilst important, the DCF calculation shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. It's not possible to obtain a foolproof valuation with a DCF model. Instead the best use for a DCF model is to test certain assumptions and theories to see if they would lead to the company being undervalued or overvalued. If a company grows at a different rate, or if its cost of equity or risk free rate changes sharply, the output can look very different. Why is the intrinsic value higher than the current share price? By conforming to environment-friendly and ethical practices, these companies can drive positive change and inspire others in the industry to follow suit.Story continuesFrom Scarcity to Success: Global Rhenium MarketThe worldwide production of Rhenium experienced a subtle decline, as the production volume dipped to approximately 59 metric tons in 2021, which decreased from the previous level of 59.3 metric tons recorded in 2020.Rhenium continues to play a vital role in jet engines and turbine blades, as well as finding applications in catalysts for oil refining within the petrochemical sector. Moreover, the healthcare industry utilizes Rhenium in various capacities, despite its overall decrease in demand.According to the "Global Rhenium Market 2022-2026" report, the Rhenium market is projected to witness substantial growth, with its market share anticipated to grow by $80.27 million by 2026. This growth is expected to occur at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.12% from 2021 to 2026. The market structure of the Rhenium industry is fragmented, with various players operating in the market.Technavio notes that the industry has shown a year-on-year growth of 12.38%, indicating a positive upward trend. In terms of regional analysis, the Rhenium market encompasses North America, Europe, APAC (Asia-Pacific), South America, and the Middle East and Africa. Among these regions, North America holds the largest market share, contributing approximately 65% to the overall market. Key consumer countries driving the demand for Rhenium include the United States, Canada, China, Russia, and Germany.Prominent Rhenium Market Trends To WatchAs the market for Rhenium continues to evolve, several key trends are expected to shape its trajectory. These trends include:Aerospace demand boost: Increasingly, Rhenium alloys are sought after in the aerospace and aviation sectors due to their heat resistance and mechanical strength.Energy sector advancements: Rhenium catalysts are gaining traction in fuel cells and hydrogen production, aligning with the growing demand for renewable energy technologies.Electronics integration: Rhenium's excellent electrical and thermal conductivity properties make it valuable in microelectronics and semiconductors, catering to the expanding electronics industry.Catalyst significance: Rhenium catalysts are finding wider applications in the chemical industry, particularly in petroleum refining, aromatics production, and catalytic reforming.Healthcare sector driving Rhenium-188 demand: The growing use of Rhenium-188 in the healthcare industry is set to generate promising opportunities for the Rhenium market in the foreseeable future.Rhenium-188 in nuclear medicine: Derived from the tungsten-188 generator, Rhenium-188 is a powerful radioisotope emitting high-energy radiation. It is extensively employed in nuclear medicine to produce radiopharmaceuticals used in therapeutic applications such as oncology, interventional radiology, cardiology, and other treatments.Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 CountriesPhoto by Artyom korshunov on UnsplashMethodologyOur assessment of Rhenium production among various countries involved a meticulous ranking methodology. To ensure the utmost reliability and accuracy of our findings, we extensively researched data from trusted sources such as The United States Geological Survey (USGS). By utilizing production percentages from E3S Web of Conferences, we calculated the production output of France and Germany specifically for the year 2020.  We then ranked the countries in ascending order according to their actual Rhenium production quantities, measured in metric tons. 10. ArmeniaMetric Tons: 0.26Armenia is known for its significant production of the rare metal Rhenium, especially for aerospace and defense industries utilization. The country's major Rhenium production is concentrated from the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine. Armenia's geological conditions and its abundant reserves of copper and molybdenum make it an ideal location for the production of Rhenium. The country's Rhenium production has played a vital role in boosting its economy and making it a significant player in the global metals market.9. KazakhstanMetric Tons: 1Kazakhstan's Rhenium production remained consistent at 1 metric ton in both 2015 and 2016, and this level was maintained in 2021 as well. The country implements a Rhenium recovery process that involves utilizing a sulphuric acid scrubbing solution. A noteworthy aspect of Kazakhstan's Rhenium production is the copper concentrates discovered in Zhezkazgan, which contain up to 30 grams per ton (g/t) of Rhenium.These deposits are globally recognized as the richest known sources of Rhenium. The abundance of Rhenium in these copper concentrates highlights the significant role played by Kazakhstan in meeting the demand for this valuable element, which finds applications in various industrial sectors.8. ChinaMetric Tons: 2.5Many producers in China have traditionally used the Kennecott Process for Rhenium extraction; there is an exception with Jiangxi Copper Corporation. The Kennecott Process has been widely used in the industry for over 40 years to extract Rhenium.In this process, exhaust gasses from the molybdenum roasting circuit are washed with water to produce perrhenic acid. The solution is then treated with chemicals like NaOH and Ca(ClO)2 to remove contaminants and adjust the pH. The solution undergoes ion exchange processing, where a resin adsorbs the Rhenium, which is later stripped using hydrochloric acid. The recovered Rhenium can further undergo purification steps, including recrystallization.Jiangxi Copper Corporation, which was the largest Rhenium producer in China in 2016, has developed and implemented its own production process. Their method includes solvent extraction of the scrubbing liquid, stripping of the organic solvent, purification, and crystallization of NH4ReO4, resulting in a Rhenium yield of up to 92%. Therefore, while the majority of Chinese producers employ the Kennecott Process, Jiangxi Copper Corporation has adopted a different approach to Rhenium recovery.7. Republic of KoreaMetric Tons: 2.8According to USGS, the Republic of Korea produced approximately 2.8 metric tons of Rhenium in 2020 and 2021. With a focus on meeting market demands and supporting various sectors, South Korea continues to contribute significantly to the production and availability of Rhenium worldwide.6. FranceMetric Tons: 4.24In 2020, France produced approximately 4.24 tons of Rhenium. The country has emerged as one of the leading producers of Rhenium products within Western Europe. This growth can be attributed to several factors, including the expansion of the aerospace industry, a thriving automotive sector, increased applications in the biomedical field, and the utilization of Rhenium powder and salt crystals. These factors have collectively contributed to the notable increase in Rhenium production within France.Click to continue reading and see Rhenium Production by Country: Top 5 Countries.Suggested Articles:10 Best Gold Royalty Stocks to Buy Now10 Small-Cap Mining Stocks Hedge Funds Are Avoiding12 Best Silver Mining Stocks To Buy NowDisclosure: none. column4: UPDATE 2-Peru bullish about copper No. 2 spot as Congo closes gap
column10: [(Adds graphic, comparative data with Congo)By Marco AquinoLIMA, June 1 (Reuters) - Peru is bullish about holding on as the world's No. 2 copper producer with key projects set to move forward, its mining minister said on Thursday amid a stern challenge from fast growing rival Democratic Republic of Congo.The Andean country has seen its position come under threat by the rapid emergence of Congo, which almost matched Peru's copper production and exports last year though it fell just short on both counts, official data from both countries show.A report earlier this week said that Congo could grab the No. 2 spot as Peru's output growth stalled within the next few years. Neighboring Andean producer Chile remains the world's dominant producer and supplier of the red metal.Both Peru and Chile have seen copper production plateau, linked to political and regulatory uncertainty.Peru's Mining Minister Oscar Vera said the country's copper industry could boost output of the key metal needed for the global electrification shift, adding that mines worth some $6 billion were set to come online over the next two years.Vera said Peru mining projects on the horizon include the $1.5 billion Zafranal mine and the $2.5 billion Yanacocha Sulfuros project controlled by Newmont Mining Corp."The general manager (of Yanacocha) was with us a few weeks ago, and we were told of their decision to continue moving forward and that they plan to invest around $400 million through the end of the year," Vera said.Newmont did not respond to a request for comment.Vera also said government authorization would be coming soon for an investment of around $1.3 billion to expand the Aluminum Corp-controlled Toromocho mine.The Andean country has some $53 billion in pending mining projects, according to government data, but most are long term and have been delayed amid social and political unrest.(Reporting by Marco Aquino; Writing by Kylie Madry; Editing by David Alire Garcia, Edmund Klamann and Chizu Nomiyama)]

column4: An Intrinsic Calculation For Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) Suggests It's 25% Undervalued
column10: [Key InsightsNewmont's estimated fair value is US$53.88 based on 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to EquityNewmont's US$40.68 share price signals that it might be 25% undervalued The US$57.12 analyst price target for NEM is 6.0% more than our estimate of fair valueHow far off is Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by projecting its future cash flows and then discounting them to today's value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Believe it or not, it's not too difficult to follow, as you'll see from our example!We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. If you still have some burning questions about this type of valuation, take a look at the Simply Wall St analysis model. View our latest analysis for Newmont The CalculationWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To begin with, we have to get estimates of the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, so we need to discount the sum of these future cash flows to arrive at a present value estimate:10-year free cash flow (FCF) estimate2023202420252026202720282029203020312032 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$1.45bUS$1.68bUS$2.20bUS$2.98bUS$3.32bUS$3.56bUS$3.77bUS$3.95bUS$4.10bUS$4.24bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x12Analyst x12Analyst x9Analyst x2Analyst x1Est @ 7.43%Est @ 5.83%Est @ 4.72%Est @ 3.93%Est @ 3.39% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 9.1% US$1.3kUS$1.4kUS$1.7kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.0kUS$2.0kUS$1.9kUS$1.8k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$18bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.1%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 9.1%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2032 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$4.2b× (1 + 2.1%) ÷ (9.1%– 2.1%) = US$62bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$62b÷ ( 1 + 9.1%)10= US$26bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$44b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$40.7, the company appears a touch undervalued at a 25% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Newmont as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 9.1%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.182. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for NewmontStrengthDebt is not viewed as a risk.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Metals and Mining market.Shareholders have been diluted in the past year.OpportunityExpected to breakeven next year.Has sufficient cash runway for more than 3 years based on current free cash flows.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatDividends are not covered by cash flow.Moving On:Whilst important, the DCF calculation shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. It's not possible to obtain a foolproof valuation with a DCF model. Instead the best use for a DCF model is to test certain assumptions and theories to see if they would lead to the company being undervalued or overvalued. If a company grows at a different rate, or if its cost of equity or risk free rate changes sharply, the output can look very different. Why is the intrinsic value higher than the current share price? column4: Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 Countries
column10: [This article explores Rhenium production by top 10 countries. You can skip the detailed industry analysis and jump straight to the Top 5 Countries by Rhenium Production.With an impressively high melting point, superb heat resistance, and extraordinary electrical conductivity, Rhenium finds extensive use in aerospace applications, where it is incorporated into high-temperature superalloys. This metal, with an atomic number of 72 and a relative atomic mass of 178.49, possesses remarkable properties that set it apart.Rhenium’s impressive melting point of 2233°C and boiling point of 4603°C make it highly resistant to extreme temperatures. With a density of 13310 kgm-3, Rhenium is known for its exceptional density among metals. Notably, it showcases a low electrical resistivity of 300 nΩm, combined with a high Young's modulus of 78 GPa, making it an ideal choice for applications requiring both electrical conductivity and mechanical strength. Furthermore, Rhenium exhibits a heat capacity of 25.73 J/K/mol. Despite its relatively low natural abundance of 5.3 ppm, Rhenium stands out with its excellent thermal conductivity of 23 W/m/K.It also serves as a catalyst in various chemical reactions and plays a vital role in advanced electronics through its application in electrical contacts. Rhenium's scarcity and specialized applications contribute to its significance in the global market.Industry leaders such as BHP Group (NYSE:BBL), Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM), and Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) can shape the future of the resources sector through sustainable practices and responsible mining. BHP Group (NYSE:BBL) operates globally in mining and petroleum, while Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) practices responsible mining worldwide. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) focuses on copper, gold, and molybdenum production. With diverse portfolios, including iron ore, copper, and coal, BHP Group (NYSE:BBL) contributes to the industry. Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) invests in communities and supplies gold. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) prioritizes safety, environmental stewardship, and community engagement. By conforming to environment-friendly and ethical practices, these companies can drive positive change and inspire others in the industry to follow suit.Story continuesFrom Scarcity to Success: Global Rhenium MarketThe worldwide production of Rhenium experienced a subtle decline, as the production volume dipped to approximately 59 metric tons in 2021, which decreased from the previous level of 59.3 metric tons recorded in 2020.Rhenium continues to play a vital role in jet engines and turbine blades, as well as finding applications in catalysts for oil refining within the petrochemical sector. Moreover, the healthcare industry utilizes Rhenium in various capacities, despite its overall decrease in demand.According to the "Global Rhenium Market 2022-2026" report, the Rhenium market is projected to witness substantial growth, with its market share anticipated to grow by $80.27 million by 2026. This growth is expected to occur at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.12% from 2021 to 2026. The market structure of the Rhenium industry is fragmented, with various players operating in the market.Technavio notes that the industry has shown a year-on-year growth of 12.38%, indicating a positive upward trend. In terms of regional analysis, the Rhenium market encompasses North America, Europe, APAC (Asia-Pacific), South America, and the Middle East and Africa. Among these regions, North America holds the largest market share, contributing approximately 65% to the overall market. Key consumer countries driving the demand for Rhenium include the United States, Canada, China, Russia, and Germany.Prominent Rhenium Market Trends To WatchAs the market for Rhenium continues to evolve, several key trends are expected to shape its trajectory. These trends include:Aerospace demand boost: Increasingly, Rhenium alloys are sought after in the aerospace and aviation sectors due to their heat resistance and mechanical strength.Energy sector advancements: Rhenium catalysts are gaining traction in fuel cells and hydrogen production, aligning with the growing demand for renewable energy technologies.Electronics integration: Rhenium's excellent electrical and thermal conductivity properties make it valuable in microelectronics and semiconductors, catering to the expanding electronics industry.Catalyst significance: Rhenium catalysts are finding wider applications in the chemical industry, particularly in petroleum refining, aromatics production, and catalytic reforming.Healthcare sector driving Rhenium-188 demand: The growing use of Rhenium-188 in the healthcare industry is set to generate promising opportunities for the Rhenium market in the foreseeable future.Rhenium-188 in nuclear medicine: Derived from the tungsten-188 generator, Rhenium-188 is a powerful radioisotope emitting high-energy radiation. It is extensively employed in nuclear medicine to produce radiopharmaceuticals used in therapeutic applications such as oncology, interventional radiology, cardiology, and other treatments.Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 CountriesPhoto by Artyom korshunov on UnsplashMethodologyOur assessment of Rhenium production among various countries involved a meticulous ranking methodology. To ensure the utmost reliability and accuracy of our findings, we extensively researched data from trusted sources such as The United States Geological Survey (USGS). By utilizing production percentages from E3S Web of Conferences, we calculated the production output of France and Germany specifically for the year 2020.  We then ranked the countries in ascending order according to their actual Rhenium production quantities, measured in metric tons. 10. ArmeniaMetric Tons: 0.26Armenia is known for its significant production of the rare metal Rhenium, especially for aerospace and defense industries utilization. The country's major Rhenium production is concentrated from the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine. Armenia's geological conditions and its abundant reserves of copper and molybdenum make it an ideal location for the production of Rhenium. The country's Rhenium production has played a vital role in boosting its economy and making it a significant player in the global metals market.9. KazakhstanMetric Tons: 1Kazakhstan's Rhenium production remained consistent at 1 metric ton in both 2015 and 2016, and this level was maintained in 2021 as well. The country implements a Rhenium recovery process that involves utilizing a sulphuric acid scrubbing solution. A noteworthy aspect of Kazakhstan's Rhenium production is the copper concentrates discovered in Zhezkazgan, which contain up to 30 grams per ton (g/t) of Rhenium.These deposits are globally recognized as the richest known sources of Rhenium. The abundance of Rhenium in these copper concentrates highlights the significant role played by Kazakhstan in meeting the demand for this valuable element, which finds applications in various industrial sectors.8. ChinaMetric Tons: 2.5Many producers in China have traditionally used the Kennecott Process for Rhenium extraction; there is an exception with Jiangxi Copper Corporation. The Kennecott Process has been widely used in the industry for over 40 years to extract Rhenium.In this process, exhaust gasses from the molybdenum roasting circuit are washed with water to produce perrhenic acid. The solution is then treated with chemicals like NaOH and Ca(ClO)2 to remove contaminants and adjust the pH. The solution undergoes ion exchange processing, where a resin adsorbs the Rhenium, which is later stripped using hydrochloric acid. The recovered Rhenium can further undergo purification steps, including recrystallization.Jiangxi Copper Corporation, which was the largest Rhenium producer in China in 2016, has developed and implemented its own production process. Their method includes solvent extraction of the scrubbing liquid, stripping of the organic solvent, purification, and crystallization of NH4ReO4, resulting in a Rhenium yield of up to 92%. Therefore, while the majority of Chinese producers employ the Kennecott Process, Jiangxi Copper Corporation has adopted a different approach to Rhenium recovery.7. Republic of KoreaMetric Tons: 2.8According to USGS, the Republic of Korea produced approximately 2.8 metric tons of Rhenium in 2020 and 2021. South Korea's production of Rhenium underscores its industrial prowess and technological advancements. The country's emphasis on innovation and research has enabled it to become a key player in the global supply chain of this valuable metal. With a focus on meeting market demands and supporting various sectors, South Korea continues to contribute significantly to the production and availability of Rhenium worldwide.6. FranceMetric Tons: 4.24In 2020, France produced approximately 4.24 tons of Rhenium. The country has emerged as one of the leading producers of Rhenium products within Western Europe. This growth can be attributed to several factors, including the expansion of the aerospace industry, a thriving automotive sector, increased applications in the biomedical field, and the utilization of Rhenium powder and salt crystals. These factors have collectively contributed to the notable increase in Rhenium production within France.Click to continue reading and see Rhenium Production by Country: Top 5 Countries.Suggested Articles:10 Best Gold Royalty Stocks to Buy Now10 Small-Cap Mining Stocks Hedge Funds Are Avoiding12 Best Silver Mining Stocks To Buy NowDisclosure: none. column4: UPDATE 2-Peru bullish about copper No. 2 spot as Congo closes gap
column10: [(Adds graphic, comparative data with Congo)By Marco AquinoLIMA, June 1 (Reuters) - Peru is bullish about holding on as the world's No. 2 copper producer with key projects set to move forward, its mining minister said on Thursday amid a stern challenge from fast growing rival Democratic Republic of Congo.The Andean country has seen its position come under threat by the rapid emergence of Congo, which almost matched Peru's copper production and exports last year though it fell just short on both counts, official data from both countries show.A report earlier this week said that Congo could grab the No. 2 spot as Peru's output growth stalled within the next few years. Neighboring Andean producer Chile remains the world's dominant producer and supplier of the red metal.Both Peru and Chile have seen copper production plateau, linked to political and regulatory uncertainty.Peru's Mining Minister Oscar Vera said the country's copper industry could boost output of the key metal needed for the global electrification shift, adding that mines worth some $6 billion were set to come online over the next two years.Vera said Peru mining projects on the horizon include the $1.5 billion Zafranal mine and the $2.5 billion Yanacocha Sulfuros project controlled by Newmont Mining Corp."The general manager (of Yanacocha) was with us a few weeks ago, and we were told of their decision to continue moving forward and that they plan to invest around $400 million through the end of the year," Vera said.Newmont did not respond to a request for comment.Vera also said government authorization would be coming soon for an investment of around $1.3 billion to expand the Aluminum Corp-controlled Toromocho mine.The Andean country has some $53 billion in pending mining projects, according to government data, but most are long term and have been delayed amid social and political unrest.(Reporting by Marco Aquino; Writing by Kylie Madry; Editing by David Alire Garcia, Edmund Klamann and Chizu Nomiyama)]

column10: [Key InsightsNewmont's estimated fair value is US$53.88 based on 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to EquityNewmont's US$40.68 share price signals that it might be 25% undervalued The US$57.12 analyst price target for NEM is 6.0% more than our estimate of fair valueHow far off is Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by projecting its future cash flows and then discounting them to today's value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Believe it or not, it's not too difficult to follow, as you'll see from our example!We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. If you still have some burning questions about this type of valuation, take a look at the Simply Wall St analysis model. View our latest analysis for Newmont The CalculationWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To begin with, we have to get estimates of the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, so we need to discount the sum of these future cash flows to arrive at a present value estimate:10-year free cash flow (FCF) estimate2023202420252026202720282029203020312032 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$1.45bUS$1.68bUS$2.20bUS$2.98bUS$3.32bUS$3.56bUS$3.77bUS$3.95bUS$4.10bUS$4.24bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x12Analyst x12Analyst x9Analyst x2Analyst x1Est @ 7.43%Est @ 5.83%Est @ 4.72%Est @ 3.93%Est @ 3.39% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 9.1% US$1.3kUS$1.4kUS$1.7kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.0kUS$2.0kUS$1.9kUS$1.8k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$18bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.1%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 9.1%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2032 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$4.2b× (1 + 2.1%) ÷ (9.1%– 2.1%) = US$62bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$62b÷ ( 1 + 9.1%)10= US$26bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$44b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$40.7, the company appears a touch undervalued at a 25% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Newmont as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 9.1%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.182. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for NewmontStrengthDebt is not viewed as a risk.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Metals and Mining market.Shareholders have been diluted in the past year.OpportunityExpected to breakeven next year.Has sufficient cash runway for more than 3 years based on current free cash flows.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatDividends are not covered by cash flow.Moving On:Whilst important, the DCF calculation shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. It's not possible to obtain a foolproof valuation with a DCF model. Instead the best use for a DCF model is to test certain assumptions and theories to see if they would lead to the company being undervalued or overvalued. If a company grows at a different rate, or if its cost of equity or risk free rate changes sharply, the output can look very different. Why is the intrinsic value higher than the current share price? column10: [This article explores Rhenium production by top 10 countries. You can skip the detailed industry analysis and jump straight to the Top 5 Countries by Rhenium Production.With an impressively high melting point, superb heat resistance, and extraordinary electrical conductivity, Rhenium finds extensive use in aerospace applications, where it is incorporated into high-temperature superalloys. This metal, with an atomic number of 72 and a relative atomic mass of 178.49, possesses remarkable properties that set it apart.Rhenium’s impressive melting point of 2233°C and boiling point of 4603°C make it highly resistant to extreme temperatures. With a density of 13310 kgm-3, Rhenium is known for its exceptional density among metals. Notably, it showcases a low electrical resistivity of 300 nΩm, combined with a high Young's modulus of 78 GPa, making it an ideal choice for applications requiring both electrical conductivity and mechanical strength. Furthermore, Rhenium exhibits a heat capacity of 25.73 J/K/mol. Despite its relatively low natural abundance of 5.3 ppm, Rhenium stands out with its excellent thermal conductivity of 23 W/m/K.It also serves as a catalyst in various chemical reactions and plays a vital role in advanced electronics through its application in electrical contacts. Rhenium's scarcity and specialized applications contribute to its significance in the global market.Industry leaders such as BHP Group (NYSE:BBL), Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM), and Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) can shape the future of the resources sector through sustainable practices and responsible mining. BHP Group (NYSE:BBL) operates globally in mining and petroleum, while Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) practices responsible mining worldwide. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) focuses on copper, gold, and molybdenum production. With diverse portfolios, including iron ore, copper, and coal, BHP Group (NYSE:BBL) contributes to the industry. Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) invests in communities and supplies gold. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX) prioritizes safety, environmental stewardship, and community engagement. By conforming to environment-friendly and ethical practices, these companies can drive positive change and inspire others in the industry to follow suit.Story continuesFrom Scarcity to Success: Global Rhenium MarketThe worldwide production of Rhenium experienced a subtle decline, as the production volume dipped to approximately 59 metric tons in 2021, which decreased from the previous level of 59.3 metric tons recorded in 2020.Rhenium continues to play a vital role in jet engines and turbine blades, as well as finding applications in catalysts for oil refining within the petrochemical sector. Moreover, the healthcare industry utilizes Rhenium in various capacities, despite its overall decrease in demand.According to the "Global Rhenium Market 2022-2026" report, the Rhenium market is projected to witness substantial growth, with its market share anticipated to grow by $80.27 million by 2026. This growth is expected to occur at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.12% from 2021 to 2026. The market structure of the Rhenium industry is fragmented, with various players operating in the market.Technavio notes that the industry has shown a year-on-year growth of 12.38%, indicating a positive upward trend. In terms of regional analysis, the Rhenium market encompasses North America, Europe, APAC (Asia-Pacific), South America, and the Middle East and Africa. Among these regions, North America holds the largest market share, contributing approximately 65% to the overall market. Key consumer countries driving the demand for Rhenium include the United States, Canada, China, Russia, and Germany.Prominent Rhenium Market Trends To WatchAs the market for Rhenium continues to evolve, several key trends are expected to shape its trajectory. These trends include:Aerospace demand boost: Increasingly, Rhenium alloys are sought after in the aerospace and aviation sectors due to their heat resistance and mechanical strength.Energy sector advancements: Rhenium catalysts are gaining traction in fuel cells and hydrogen production, aligning with the growing demand for renewable energy technologies.Electronics integration: Rhenium's excellent electrical and thermal conductivity properties make it valuable in microelectronics and semiconductors, catering to the expanding electronics industry.Catalyst significance: Rhenium catalysts are finding wider applications in the chemical industry, particularly in petroleum refining, aromatics production, and catalytic reforming.Healthcare sector driving Rhenium-188 demand: The growing use of Rhenium-188 in the healthcare industry is set to generate promising opportunities for the Rhenium market in the foreseeable future.Rhenium-188 in nuclear medicine: Derived from the tungsten-188 generator, Rhenium-188 is a powerful radioisotope emitting high-energy radiation. It is extensively employed in nuclear medicine to produce radiopharmaceuticals used in therapeutic applications such as oncology, interventional radiology, cardiology, and other treatments.Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 CountriesPhoto by Artyom korshunov on UnsplashMethodologyOur assessment of Rhenium production among various countries involved a meticulous ranking methodology. To ensure the utmost reliability and accuracy of our findings, we extensively researched data from trusted sources such as The United States Geological Survey (USGS). By utilizing production percentages from E3S Web of Conferences, we calculated the production output of France and Germany specifically for the year 2020.  We then ranked the countries in ascending order according to their actual Rhenium production quantities, measured in metric tons. 10. ArmeniaMetric Tons: 0.26Armenia is known for its significant production of the rare metal Rhenium, especially for aerospace and defense industries utilization. The country's major Rhenium production is concentrated from the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine. Armenia's geological conditions and its abundant reserves of copper and molybdenum make it an ideal location for the production of Rhenium. The country's Rhenium production has played a vital role in boosting its economy and making it a significant player in the global metals market.9. KazakhstanMetric Tons: 1Kazakhstan's Rhenium production remained consistent at 1 metric ton in both 2015 and 2016, and this level was maintained in 2021 as well. The country implements a Rhenium recovery process that involves utilizing a sulphuric acid scrubbing solution. A noteworthy aspect of Kazakhstan's Rhenium production is the copper concentrates discovered in Zhezkazgan, which contain up to 30 grams per ton (g/t) of Rhenium.These deposits are globally recognized as the richest known sources of Rhenium. The abundance of Rhenium in these copper concentrates highlights the significant role played by Kazakhstan in meeting the demand for this valuable element, which finds applications in various industrial sectors.8. ChinaMetric Tons: 2.5Many producers in China have traditionally used the Kennecott Process for Rhenium extraction; there is an exception with Jiangxi Copper Corporation. The Kennecott Process has been widely used in the industry for over 40 years to extract Rhenium.In this process, exhaust gasses from the molybdenum roasting circuit are washed with water to produce perrhenic acid. The solution is then treated with chemicals like NaOH and Ca(ClO)2 to remove contaminants and adjust the pH. The solution undergoes ion exchange processing, where a resin adsorbs the Rhenium, which is later stripped using hydrochloric acid. The recovered Rhenium can further undergo purification steps, including recrystallization.Jiangxi Copper Corporation, which was the largest Rhenium producer in China in 2016, has developed and implemented its own production process. Their method includes solvent extraction of the scrubbing liquid, stripping of the organic solvent, purification, and crystallization of NH4ReO4, resulting in a Rhenium yield of up to 92%. Therefore, while the majority of Chinese producers employ the Kennecott Process, Jiangxi Copper Corporation has adopted a different approach to Rhenium recovery.7. Republic of KoreaMetric Tons: 2.8According to USGS, the Republic of Korea produced approximately 2.8 metric tons of Rhenium in 2020 and 2021. South Korea's production of Rhenium underscores its industrial prowess and technological advancements. The country's emphasis on innovation and research has enabled it to become a key player in the global supply chain of this valuable metal. With a focus on meeting market demands and supporting various sectors, South Korea continues to contribute significantly to the production and availability of Rhenium worldwide.6. FranceMetric Tons: 4.24In 2020, France produced approximately 4.24 tons of Rhenium. The country has emerged as one of the leading producers of Rhenium products within Western Europe. This growth can be attributed to several factors, including the expansion of the aerospace industry, a thriving automotive sector, increased applications in the biomedical field, and the utilization of Rhenium powder and salt crystals. These factors have collectively contributed to the notable increase in Rhenium production within France.Click to continue reading and see Rhenium Production by Country: Top 5 Countries.Suggested Articles:10 Best Gold Royalty Stocks to Buy Now10 Small-Cap Mining Stocks Hedge Funds Are Avoiding12 Best Silver Mining Stocks To Buy NowDisclosure: none. column4: UPDATE 2-Peru bullish about copper No. 2 spot as Congo closes gap
column10: [(Adds graphic, comparative data with Congo)By Marco AquinoLIMA, June 1 (Reuters) - Peru is bullish about holding on as the world's No. 2 copper producer with key projects set to move forward, its mining minister said on Thursday amid a stern challenge from fast growing rival Democratic Republic of Congo.The Andean country has seen its position come under threat by the rapid emergence of Congo, which almost matched Peru's copper production and exports last year though it fell just short on both counts, official data from both countries show.A report earlier this week said that Congo could grab the No. 2 spot as Peru's output growth stalled within the next few years. Neighboring Andean producer Chile remains the world's dominant producer and supplier of the red metal.Both Peru and Chile have seen copper production plateau, linked to political and regulatory uncertainty.Peru's Mining Minister Oscar Vera said the country's copper industry could boost output of the key metal needed for the global electrification shift, adding that mines worth some $6 billion were set to come online over the next two years.Vera said Peru mining projects on the horizon include the $1.5 billion Zafranal mine and the $2.5 billion Yanacocha Sulfuros project controlled by Newmont Mining Corp."The general manager (of Yanacocha) was with us a few weeks ago, and we were told of their decision to continue moving forward and that they plan to invest around $400 million through the end of the year," Vera said.Newmont did not respond to a request for comment.Vera also said government authorization would be coming soon for an investment of around $1.3 billion to expand the Aluminum Corp-controlled Toromocho mine.The Andean country has some $53 billion in pending mining projects, according to government data, but most are long term and have been delayed amid social and political unrest.(Reporting by Marco Aquino; Writing by Kylie Madry; Editing by David Alire Garcia, Edmund Klamann and Chizu Nomiyama)]

column4: An Intrinsic Calculation For Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) Suggests It's 25% Undervalued
column10: [Key InsightsNewmont's estimated fair value is US$53.88 based on 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to EquityNewmont's US$40.68 share price signals that it might be 25% undervalued The US$57.12 analyst price target for NEM is 6.0% more than our estimate of fair valueHow far off is Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by projecting its future cash flows and then discounting them to today's value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Believe it or not, it's not too difficult to follow, as you'll see from our example!We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. If you still have some burning questions about this type of valuation, take a look at the Simply Wall St analysis model. View our latest analysis for Newmont The CalculationWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To begin with, we have to get estimates of the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, so we need to discount the sum of these future cash flows to arrive at a present value estimate:10-year free cash flow (FCF) estimate2023202420252026202720282029203020312032 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$1.45bUS$1.68bUS$2.20bUS$2.98bUS$3.32bUS$3.56bUS$3.77bUS$3.95bUS$4.10bUS$4.24bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x12Analyst x12Analyst x9Analyst x2Analyst x1Est @ 7.43%Est @ 5.83%Est @ 4.72%Est @ 3.93%Est @ 3.39% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 9.1% US$1.3kUS$1.4kUS$1.7kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.1kUS$2.0kUS$2.0kUS$1.9kUS$1.8k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$18bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.1%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 9.1%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2032 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$4.2b× (1 + 2.1%) ÷ (9.1%– 2.1%) = US$62bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$62b÷ ( 1 + 9.1%)10= US$26bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$44b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$40.7, the company appears a touch undervalued at a 25% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Newmont as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 9.1%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.182. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for NewmontStrengthDebt is not viewed as a risk.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Metals and Mining market.Shareholders have been diluted in the past year.OpportunityExpected to breakeven next year.Has sufficient cash runway for more than 3 years based on current free cash flows.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatDividends are not covered by cash flow.Moving On:Whilst important, the DCF calculation shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. It's not possible to obtain a foolproof valuation with a DCF model. Instead the best use for a DCF model is to test certain assumptions and theories to see if they would lead to the company being undervalued or overvalued. If a company grows at a different rate, or if its cost of equity or risk free rate changes sharply, the output can look very different. Why is the intrinsic value higher than the current share price? This metal, with an atomic number of 72 and a relative atomic mass of 178.49, possesses remarkable properties that set it apart.Rhenium’s impressive melting point of 2233°C and boiling point of 4603°C make it highly resistant to extreme temperatures. With a density of 13310 kgm-3, Rhenium is known for its exceptional density among metals. Notably, it showcases a low electrical resistivity of 300 nΩm, combined with a high Young's modulus of 78 GPa, making it an ideal choice for applications requiring both electrical conductivity and mechanical strength. Furthermore, Rhenium exhibits a heat capacity of 25.73 J/K/mol. Despite its relatively low natural abundance of 5.3 ppm, Rhenium stands out with its excellent thermal conductivity of 23 W/m/K.It also serves as a catalyst in various chemical reactions and plays a vital role in advanced electronics through its application in electrical contacts. Rhenium's scarcity and specialized applications contribute to its significance in the global market.Industry leaders such as BHP Group (NYSE:BBL), Newmont Corporation (NYSE:NEM), and Freeport-McMoRan Inc. Moreover, the healthcare industry utilizes Rhenium in various capacities, despite its overall decrease in demand.According to the "Global Rhenium Market 2022-2026" report, the Rhenium market is projected to witness substantial growth, with its market share anticipated to grow by $80.27 million by 2026. This growth is expected to occur at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.12% from 2021 to 2026. The market structure of the Rhenium industry is fragmented, with various players operating in the market.Technavio notes that the industry has shown a year-on-year growth of 12.38%, indicating a positive upward trend. In terms of regional analysis, the Rhenium market encompasses North America, Europe, APAC (Asia-Pacific), South America, and the Middle East and Africa. Among these regions, North America holds the largest market share, contributing approximately 65% to the overall market. Key consumer countries driving the demand for Rhenium include the United States, Canada, China, Russia, and Germany.Prominent Rhenium Market Trends To WatchAs the market for Rhenium continues to evolve, several key trends are expected to shape its trajectory. These trends include:Aerospace demand boost: Increasingly, Rhenium alloys are sought after in the aerospace and aviation sectors due to their heat resistance and mechanical strength.Energy sector advancements: Rhenium catalysts are gaining traction in fuel cells and hydrogen production, aligning with the growing demand for renewable energy technologies.Electronics integration: Rhenium's excellent electrical and thermal conductivity properties make it valuable in microelectronics and semiconductors, catering to the expanding electronics industry.Catalyst significance: Rhenium catalysts are finding wider applications in the chemical industry, particularly in petroleum refining, aromatics production, and catalytic reforming.Healthcare sector driving Rhenium-188 demand: The growing use of Rhenium-188 in the healthcare industry is set to generate promising opportunities for the Rhenium market in the foreseeable future.Rhenium-188 in nuclear medicine: Derived from the tungsten-188 generator, Rhenium-188 is a powerful radioisotope emitting high-energy radiation. It is extensively employed in nuclear medicine to produce radiopharmaceuticals used in therapeutic applications such as oncology, interventional radiology, cardiology, and other treatments.Rhenium Production by Country: Top 10 CountriesPhoto by Artyom korshunov on UnsplashMethodologyOur assessment of Rhenium production among various countries involved a meticulous ranking methodology. To ensure the utmost reliability and accuracy of our findings, we extensively researched data from trusted sources such as The United States Geological Survey (USGS). By utilizing production percentages from E3S Web of Conferences, we calculated the production output of France and Germany specifically for the year 2020.  We then ranked the countries in ascending order according to their actual Rhenium production quantities, measured in metric tons. 10. ArmeniaMetric Tons: 0.26Armenia is known for its significant production of the rare metal Rhenium, especially for aerospace and defense industries utilization. The country's major Rhenium production is concentrated from the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine. Armenia's geological conditions and its abundant reserves of copper and molybdenum make it an ideal location for the production of Rhenium. The country's Rhenium production has played a vital role in boosting its economy and making it a significant player in the global metals market.9. KazakhstanMetric Tons: 1Kazakhstan's Rhenium production remained consistent at 1 metric ton in both 2015 and 2016, and this level was maintained in 2021 as well. The country implements a Rhenium recovery process that involves utilizing a sulphuric acid scrubbing solution. A noteworthy aspect of Kazakhstan's Rhenium production is the copper concentrates discovered in Zhezkazgan, which contain up to 30 grams per ton (g/t) of Rhenium.These deposits are globally recognized as the richest known sources of Rhenium. The abundance of Rhenium in these copper concentrates highlights the significant role played by Kazakhstan in meeting the demand for this valuable element, which finds applications in various industrial sectors.8. ChinaMetric Tons: 2.5Many producers in China have traditionally used the Kennecott Process for Rhenium extraction; there is an exception with Jiangxi Copper Corporation. The Kennecott Process has been widely used in the industry for over 40 years to extract Rhenium.In this process, exhaust gasses from the molybdenum roasting circuit are washed with water to produce perrhenic acid. The solution is then treated with chemicals like NaOH and Ca(ClO)2 to remove contaminants and adjust the pH. The solution undergoes ion exchange processing, where a resin adsorbs the Rhenium, which is later stripped using hydrochloric acid. The recovered Rhenium can further undergo purification steps, including recrystallization.Jiangxi Copper Corporation, which was the largest Rhenium producer in China in 2016, has developed and implemented its own production process. Their method includes solvent extraction of the scrubbing liquid, stripping of the organic solvent, purification, and crystallization of NH4ReO4, resulting in a Rhenium yield of up to 92%. Therefore, while the majority of Chinese producers employ the Kennecott Process, Jiangxi Copper Corporation has adopted a different approach to Rhenium recovery.7. Republic of KoreaMetric Tons: 2.8According to USGS, the Republic of Korea produced approximately 2.8 metric tons of Rhenium in 2020 and 2021. The country's emphasis on innovation and research has enabled it to become a key player in the global supply chain of this valuable metal. With a focus on meeting market demands and supporting various sectors, South Korea continues to contribute significantly to the production and availability of Rhenium worldwide.6. FranceMetric Tons: 4.24In 2020, France produced approximately 4.24 tons of Rhenium. The country has emerged as one of the leading producers of Rhenium products within Western Europe. This growth can be attributed to several factors, including the expansion of the aerospace industry, a thriving automotive sector, increased applications in the biomedical field, and the utilization of Rhenium powder and salt crystals. column4: UPDATE 2-Peru bullish about copper No. 2 spot as Congo closes gap
column10: [(Adds graphic, comparative data with Congo)By Marco AquinoLIMA, June 1 (Reuters) - Peru is bullish about holding on as the world's No. 2 copper producer with key projects set to move forward, its mining minister said on Thursday amid a stern challenge from fast growing rival Democratic Republic of Congo.The Andean country has seen its position come under threat by the rapid emergence of Congo, which almost matched Peru's copper production and exports last year though it fell just short on both counts, official data from both countries show.A report earlier this week said that Congo could grab the No. 2 spot as Peru's output growth stalled within the next few years. Neighboring Andean producer Chile remains the world's dominant producer and supplier of the red metal.Both Peru and Chile have seen copper production plateau, linked to political and regulatory uncertainty.Peru's Mining Minister Oscar Vera said the country's copper industry could boost output of the key metal needed for the global electrification shift, adding that mines worth some $6 billion were set to come online over the next two years.Vera said Peru mining projects on the horizon include the $1.5 billion Zafranal mine and the $2.5 billion Yanacocha Sulfuros project controlled by Newmont Mining Corp."The general manager (of Yanacocha) was with us a few weeks ago, and we were told of their decision to continue moving forward and that they plan to invest around $400 million through the end of the year," Vera said.Newmont did not respond to a request for comment.Vera also said government authorization would be coming soon for an investment of around $1.3 billion to expand the Aluminum Corp-controlled Toromocho mine.The Andean country has some $53 billion in pending mining projects, according to government data, but most are long term and have been delayed amid social and political unrest.(Reporting by Marco Aquino; Writing by Kylie Madry; Editing by David Alire Garcia, Edmund Klamann and Chizu Nomiyama)]

According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.Story continuesZacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.It has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts issue more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them.In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates.
